sources.title: Matrix region-sum writer fixture plus actual-candidate independent oracle

claims.text: The preserved source identifies immutable 2D region-sum / LeetCode 304 without preserving Java-specific API, numeric width, or invalid-input contracts.
The actual candidate constructs a 2D prefix table and answers inclusive sub-rectangles by four-term inclusion-exclusion.
Independent checks confirm snapshot immutability, long accumulation, rectangular-input enforcement and invalid-region rejection under the explicit answer-side contract.
The implementation fills one (R+1)x(C+1) table once and each query reads four entries, matching O(RC) preprocessing/space and O(1) query time.

findings: The exact repository source identifies the immutable two-dimensional region-sum problem and preserves the LeetCode 304 context; it does not preserve Java API, numeric-width, invalid-input, or mutation-after-construction contracts.
The candidate keeps those unstated API choices explicit as answer-side contracts instead of presenting them as recovered source requirements.
The two-dimensional prefix recurrence and four-term inclusion-exclusion query are internally consistent, including the +1 sentinel row/column convention and inclusive query endpoints.
Independent review compiles and runs the actual candidate against a direct nested-loop oracle over exhaustive small matrices and 100,000 deterministic randomized regions.
Snapshot immutability, long accumulation beyond int range, jagged/empty input rejection, and invalid-region rejection are independently exercised and match the candidate text.
O(RC) preprocessing/space and O(1) query claims match the implementation structure; the answer correctly separates mutable-matrix alternatives as a different contract.
